stops.title: Arrive Narita Airport Terminal 2
stops.notes: TICKETED (Cathay, PNR ECPN6Z): CX672 HYD 02:05 → HKG 09:40, CX500 HKG 15:25 → NRT T2 20:20. Economy Light: 1×23 kg checked + 7 kg cabin each.
stops.blurb: Narita is Tokyo's main international gateway, about 60–90 minutes east of the city; Terminal 2 is Cathay Pacific's home and the first stamp of the trip.

stops.title: Private car to the hotel — check-in & sleep
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.notes: private car, ~90 min to central Tokyo — booked for ~21:15, after immigration and bags
stops.transit: Pre-booked private car, driver meets you at T2 arrivals with a name board ~21:15 — ~75–80 min door to door to Higashi-Kanda. Fallback if the car falls through: JR Narita Express to Tokyo Stn (~55 min) + 10-min taxi, last N'EX ~21:44.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.notes: booked base — Higashi-Kanda, JR Bakurocho 350 m

stops.title: JR Asakusabashi Station
stops.transit: Walk 10 min from the hotel, up the Kiyosubashi-dori side streets, to JR Asakusabashi.

stops.title: Sumo wrestling experience
stops.notes: approximate — venue not named; Ryogoku Kokugikan area
stops.blurb: Ryogoku is the historic heartland of sumo, home to the Kokugikan national stadium and the training stables where visitors can watch wrestlers' intense morning practice.
stops.transit: Chuo-Sobu Local (yellow, toward Chiba) 1 stop to Ryogoku, ¥150 pp — West exit faces the Kokugikan. (Or skip the train: it's a 20-min walk all the way.)

stops.title: Toei Oedo Ryogoku Station
stops.transit: 2-min walk from the Kokugikan to Toei Oedo Ryogoku station.

stops.title: Asakusa and Senso-ji Temple
stops.blurb: Senso-ji is Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 628 AD and dedicated to the bodhisattva Kannon, famed for the giant red lantern of its Kaminarimon gate.
stops.transit: Toei Oedo Line 1 stop to Kuramae, 4-min street walk to the Kuramae Asakusa-Line platform, then 1 stop to Asakusa, exit 1 — ~20 min, ¥180 pp. (Lazy option: 8-min taxi, ~¥1,100.)

stops.title: Free time on Nakamise Shopping Street
stops.blurb: Nakamise is the centuries-old shopping street leading to Senso-ji, lined since the Edo period with nearly a hundred stalls selling traditional snacks, crafts and souvenirs.
stops.transit: 2-min walk — Nakamise IS the approach street from Senso-ji's Hozomon gate back toward Kaminarimon.

stops.title: Skytree base & Solamachi — no ascent
stops.notes: Ground level only — Solamachi mall + looking up. We go UP the tower on Day 15 night (1 Jan). Skip the ticket queue today.
stops.blurb: Tokyo Skytree is Japan's tallest structure at 634 metres, a broadcasting tower with twin observation decks offering panoramic views across the Kanto plain to Mt. Fuji.
stops.transit: Walk it: 20 min east over the Sumida River (Azumabashi bridge, riverside path) with Skytree in view the whole way — or Tobu Skytree Line Asakusa → Tokyo Skytree, 1 stop, 3 min, ¥160.

stops.title: Oshiage Station (Asakusa line)
stops.transit: Escalators down — Skytree's basement IS Oshiage station (Asakusa-line platforms).

stops.title: Return to hotel and rest
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.notes: booked base — Higashi-Kanda, JR Bakurocho 350 m
stops.transit: Toei Asakusa Line (toward Nishi-magome) → Higashi-Nihombashi, ~15 min, ¥220 pp; then an 8-min walk home.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.notes: booked base — Higashi-Kanda, JR Bakurocho 350 m

stops.title: Higashi-Nihombashi Station (Asakusa line)
stops.transit: 8-min walk from the hotel to Higashi-Nihombashi station.

stops.title: Kabukiza facade photo
stops.notes: exterior only, 15–20 min; walk Harumi-dori to the Ginza spine
stops.blurb: Kabuki-za (Kabukiza Theatre) is a historic performing arts venue in Tokyo's Ginza district dedicated to traditional Japanese Kabuki theater.
stops.transit: Toei Asakusa Line (toward Nishi-magome) direct to Higashi-Ginza, ~11 min, ¥220 pp — Kabukiza sits on exit 3.

stops.title: G.Itoya flagship — quick hit
stops.notes: Sun 10:00–19:00; 25 min on floors 1–2 — full 12-floor browse on 2 Jan
stops.blurb: G.Itoya is Ginza's legendary stationery emporium, founded in 1904, whose 12-floor flagship is a pilgrimage site for pens, paper and fine Japanese writing goods.
stops.transit: 5-min walk north up Chuo-dori to 2-chome — Itoya's red-paperclip sign on the right.

stops.title: Wako Seiko clock tower — 10:30 chime
stops.notes: Westminster chime on the hour since 1954 — photo at the crossing, 1 min to museum
stops.blurb: The Wako building's Seiko clock tower, rebuilt in 1932, is the defining landmark of Ginza's 4-chome crossing, sounding Westminster chimes on the hour since 1954.
stops.transit: 4-min walk back down Chuo-dori to the 4-chome crossing — be under the Wako clock just before 10:30.

stops.title: Seiko Museum Ginza
stops.notes: opens 10:30 (NOT 10:00) — free, reserve the first slot online; 45 min
stops.blurb: The Seiko Museum Ginza traces the watchmaker's history from founder Kintaro Hattori's 1881 shop, displaying Japan's first wristwatches and the Grand Seiko lineage.
stops.transit: 1-min walk — the museum entrance is on the side street directly behind Wako.

stops.title: Seiko Dream Square — buy his SARJ011
stops.notes: Core Shop exclusive; tax-free ≈¥145,000; 60 min incl. paperwork
stops.blurb: Seiko Dream Square is the brand's flagship boutique steps from the Ginza crossing, showcasing the full Seiko and Grand Seiko collections including shop-exclusive models.
stops.transit: 2-min walk across to 4-4-10 Ginza — Dream Square is Seiko's own retail floor.

stops.title: Kimuraya Honten — warm 1874 anpan
stops.notes: anpan invented here 1874 (~¥200); eat walking the car-free Chuo-dori (Sun 12:00–17:00)
stops.blurb: Ginza Kimuraya is the bakery that invented the anpan — a sake-yeast bun filled with sweet red-bean paste — in 1874, later presented to the Emperor.
stops.transit: 1-min walk back to the 4-chome crossing corner — Kimuraya has sold anpan here since 1874.

stops.title: NISSAN CROSSING (optional, 10 min)
stops.notes: free 2-floor showroom on the same corner — Formula E GEN3 Evo (Tokyo E-Prix livery) + GT-R T-spec; exhibits rotate — only if ahead of schedule, Bic by 12:40
stops.blurb: Nissan Crossing is the carmaker's glassy two-floor brand showroom on Ginza's 4-chome crossing, displaying rotating concept, racing and heritage cars.
stops.transit: It's the glass corner ON the crossing — 30 seconds. Ten minutes max, it's a showroom.

stops.title: Bic Camera Yurakucho — her Orient Star + his iPhone 18 Pro
stops.notes: iPhone 18 Pro 512GB: SIM-free at Apple's list ¥254,800 — buy HERE at the tax-free counter with passport (~¥23,200 refunded to card via the new system), NOT at Apple Ginza (Apple stopped tax-free in 2022). Check bic camera stock that morning. Japan model = eSIM-only + shutter sound (goes silent outside Japan). Her Orient Star lives on the watch floor.
stops.blurb: Bic Camera Yurakucho is a vast multi-floor electronics megastore whose watch department carries major Japanese brands including Seiko and Orient Star at tax-free prices.
stops.transit: 7-min walk up Harumi-dori toward Yurakucho Stn — Bic Camera is the big block at the station end. Her Orient Star lives on the watch floor.

stops.title: Lunch — Tricolore Honten (est. 1936)
stops.notes: no bookings, 10–25 min Sunday wait; vegetarian-workable; backup: Café Paulista (1911)
stops.blurb: Tricolore Honten, founded in 1936, is a classic Showa-era Ginza kissaten known for its antique interior, hand nel-dripped coffee and famous eclair.
stops.transit: 8-min walk back into Ginza 5-chome — Tricolore's brick alley entrance is off Namiki-dori.

stops.title: UNIQLO Ginza — 12-floor flagship
stops.notes: hard stop 14:55 → Ginza Stn A2 → Ginza line to Shibuya (~16 min)
stops.blurb: UNIQLO Ginza is the brand's 12-floor global flagship and one of the world's largest UNIQLO stores, stocking flagship-exclusive lines and the full UT collection.
stops.transit: 4-min walk down Chuo-dori to 6-chome — all 12 floors; parka and Heattech run happens HERE (cheaper than India, tax-free over ¥5,000).

stops.title: Ginza Station (Ginza line)
stops.transit: Ginza Stn is right under the 4-chome crossing — follow the orange G signs to platform 1.

stops.title: Shibuya Sky — sunset slot
stops.notes: ~¥2,600 pp; tickets ~6 Dec 00:00 JST; sunset 16:32
stops.blurb: Shibuya Sky is the 229-metre open-air observatory atop Shibuya Scramble Square, looking straight down on the world's busiest pedestrian crossing.
stops.transit: Tokyo Metro Ginza Line (toward Shibuya) — ride to the TERMINUS, 16 min, ¥210 pp, tap Suica. The platform at Shibuya is on the 3rd floor of Shibuya Scramble Square itself — the Shibuya Sky elevators (14F) are in the same building.

stops.title: Hachiko + Shibuya Crossing
stops.notes: the Scramble is right here — Starbucks Tsutaya 2F / Mag's Park for the overhead shot
stops.blurb: The Hachiko statue honours the Akita dog who waited at Shibuya Station daily for nine years after his owner's death, beside the famous scramble crossing.
stops.transit: Ride the escalators down to ground level — Hachiko exit. 3 minutes, follow the crowd.

stops.title: Shibuya dinner
stops.transit: Walk — everything from izakaya to Ichiran is within 5 min of the crossing.

stops.title: Shibuya Station (Ginza line)
stops.transit: Back into Shibuya Scramble Square, 3rd floor — the Ginza Line starts here.

stops.title: Back at the hotel — night in
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.transit: Ginza Line (it's the terminus — you'll get seats) → Nihombashi, ~22 min, ¥260 pp; cross to the Toei Asakusa Line, 2 stops to Higashi-Nihombashi; 8-min walk home. ~45 min door to door.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.notes: booked base — Higashi-Kanda, JR Bakurocho 350 m

stops.title: JR Bakurocho Station
stops.transit: 4-min walk from the hotel to JR Bakurocho — the platforms are deep, allow a couple of extra minutes.

stops.title: Maihama Station — Disney Resort Line
stops.notes: change to the Disney monorail here
stops.transit: JR Sobu Rapid 1 stop to Tokyo Stn → follow the Keiyo Line signs (10-min walk inside the station) → Maihama, 16 min. ~¥530 pp.

stops.title: Tokyo DisneySea experience
stops.blurb: Tokyo DisneySea is a nautical-themed Disney park found only in Tokyo, widely regarded as one of the most beautifully designed theme parks in the world.
stops.transit: Disney Resort Line monorail Maihama → Tokyo DisneySea Stn, ~10 min, ¥300 pp — buy the return ticket now to skip the closing queue.

stops.title: Tokyo DisneySea Station (monorail)
stops.transit: 5-min walk from the park gates up to the monorail station.

stops.title: Back at the hotel — DisneySea day done
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.notes: booked base — Higashi-Kanda, JR Bakurocho 350 m
stops.transit: Disney Resort Line monorail → Maihama (¥300, ticket bought in the morning), then JR Keiyo to Tokyo Stn → Sobu Rapid 1 stop to Bakurocho, 4-min walk home.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.notes: booked base — Higashi-Kanda, JR Bakurocho 350 m

stops.title: Hotel check-out
stops.place: Comfort Hotel ERA Tokyo Higashi Kanda
stops.notes: Big suitcases DON'T come today: ERA's desk ships them by takkyubin to the Kyoto hotel this morning (~¥2,500/bag, arrives before you do on 24 Dec) — one overnight bag each for the Fuji + Kanazawa nights.

stops.title: JR Asakusabashi Station
stops.transit: Walk 10 min from the hotel to JR Asakusabashi.

stops.title: Shinjuku Station — limited-express platforms
stops.notes: the Fuji Excursion (reserved, ~¥4,130 pp) leaves from here — direct to Shimoyoshida
stops.blurb: Arakurayama Sengen Park is a hillside shrine park in Fujiyoshida whose pagoda-and-Mt.-Fuji panorama is one of Japan's most famous postcard views.
stops.transit: Chuo-Sobu Local (yellow) direct to Shinjuku, ~25 min, ¥230 pp; inside Shinjuku follow the limited-express signs to the Fuji Excursion platforms, ~8 min.

stops.title: Chureito Pagoda, Mt. Fuji views
stops.notes: approximate — pagoda sits ~400 steps uphill within Arakurayama Sengen Park
stops.blurb: The Chureito Pagoda is a five-storey vermilion pagoda whose terrace frames Mt. Fuji in Japan's classic postcard composition, reached by a climb of about 400 steps.
stops.transit: Fuji Excursion (reserved) Shinjuku → Shimoyoshida direct, ~1h55m; off at Shimoyoshida — one small exit, follow the Chureito Pagoda signs: 15-min gentle uphill through town, then the 398 steps to the pagoda deck — Fuji behind you the whole climb.

stops.title: Shimoyoshida Station (Fujikyu)
stops.transit: Back down from the pagoda — 398 steps + 12-min downhill to Shimoyoshida Stn.

stops.title: Kawaguchiko Station
stops.transit: Fujikyu local line → Kawaguchiko, 15 min, ¥310 pp.

stops.title: Lake Kawaguchi sightseeing boat experience
stops.notes: approximate — Funatsu pier next to the Kawaguchiko ropeway
stops.blurb: Lake Kawaguchi is the most accessible of the Fuji Five Lakes, and its sightseeing cruise offers sweeping water-level views of Mt. Fuji from the northern foothills.
stops.transit: From Kawaguchiko Stn: 15-min lakeside walk to the boat pier, or a 5-min taxi (~¥1,000).

stops.title: Hotel pickup → Mizno check-in
stops.notes: Mizno Hotel — check in, then the evening is yours: book the rooftop private-bath slot at the desk FIRST thing, dinner at SEIKOUKI from 18:30
stops.transit: From the pier, call Mizno for pickup (0555-72-1234, 5–10 min) or take a ~¥1,500 taxi — the hotel sits up a steep hill above Asakawa on the north-east shore; don't try to walk it with bags.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.notes: Mizno Hotel — every room faces Fuji over the lake; private rooftop onsen for two; the anniversary night

stops.title: Oishi Park — sunrise Fuji light
stops.blurb: Oishi Park on Lake Kawaguchi's northern shore is celebrated for its unobstructed lake-and-Fuji panorama, among the finest viewpoints in the Fuji Five Lakes region.
stops.transit: Taxi, booked the night before at Mizno's front desk — ~10 min around the lake's north shore from Asakawa, ~¥1,500–1,800 total. (Buses don't make a 07:45 sunrise.)

stops.title: Hotel check-out
stops.notes: Mizno Hotel — every room faces Fuji over the lake; private rooftop onsen for two; the anniversary night
stops.transit: Same taxi back from Oishi Park — ask the driver to wait (10 min each way, ~¥3,500 round trip) or have Mizno's desk book the return the night before.

stops.title: Kawaguchiko Station — shuttle drop
stops.transit: Free Mizno shuttle to the station — every 30 min, 08:00–11:00, no reservation needed (or ~¥1,500 taxi).

stops.title: Tokyo Station — Hokuriku Shinkansen gates
stops.notes: change here for the ~12:20 Kagayaki to Kanazawa
stops.blurb: Kawaguchiko Station is the gateway terminus of the Fuji Five Lakes region, linked to Tokyo by the direct Fuji Excursion limited express and highway buses.
stops.transit: Fuji Excursion (reserved) Kawaguchiko → Shinjuku, ~1h55m, ¥4,130 pp; stay inside the JR gates, cross to the Chuo Rapid platform (~5 min) → Tokyo Stn, 14 min, ¥210; then follow the blue Hokuriku Shinkansen signs ~10 min to the gates.

stops.title: Kanazawa Station — arrival
stops.notes: take the EAST (Kenrokuen) exit — under the wooden Tsuzumi-mon drum gate
stops.blurb: Kanazawa Station's Tsuzumi-mon gate, shaped like two hand-drums, is routinely ranked among the world's most beautiful station entrances.
stops.transit: Kagayaki Shinkansen (all reserved) Tokyo → Kanazawa, 2h28m · ¥14,380 pp (Eki-net Tokudane early-bird cuts up to 30%; luggage racks at car ends, no oversized rule); arrive ~14:50 at Kanazawa Station.

stops.title: Hotel Forza check-in
stops.notes: book the Comfort or Refresh Double (18 m², 150 cm bed) — the base “Forza Double” bed is 140 cm
stops.transit: Out of the EAST (Kenrokuen) exit, straight down Hyakumangoku-odori — 10-min flat walk; Hotel Forza stands beside Omicho Market. (Taxi rank at the exit if bags feel heavy, ~¥600.)

stops.title: Musashigatsuji · Omicho bus stop
stops.transit: 3-min walk from the hotel to the Musashigatsuji · Omicho bus stop.

stops.title: Kenrokuen — yukitsuri snow-ropes
stops.blurb: Kenrokuen is one of Japan's three great landscape gardens, famed in winter for yukitsuri — conical rope supports that protect its ancient pines from heavy snow.
stops.transit: Kanazawa Loop Bus (Right Loop) → Kenrokuen-shita, ~10 min, ¥210 — or skip the bus: a 25-min walk up through the castle park.

stops.title: Higashi Chaya district stroll
stops.blurb: Higashi Chaya is Kanazawa's largest preserved geisha district, its Edo-period wooden teahouses now housing gold-leaf shops and cafes along lantern-lit lanes.
stops.transit: 15-min downhill walk via Hashiba-cho — or Loop Bus RL two stops to Hashiba-cho; the chaya streets start 3 min from the stop.

stops.title: Hashiba-cho bus stop
stops.transit: 3-min walk from the chaya streets to the Hashiba-cho bus stop.

stops.title: Dinner + Christmas illuminations, Katamachi
stops.blurb: Katamachi is Kanazawa's main shopping and nightlife district, whose landmark Christmas tree illumination doubles as a yukitsuri light display through the winter.
stops.transit: Loop Bus (Left Loop) toward Korinbo/Katamachi, ~12 min, ¥210 — or a 20-min riverside walk along the Asano. Dinner street is Katamachi Chuo-dori.

stops.title: Katamachi bus stop
stops.transit: The Katamachi stop is on Chuo-dori, by the main crossing.

stops.title: Back at Forza — night in
stops.transit: Any Hokutetsu bus toward Kanazawa Stn, 4 stops to Musashigatsuji·Omicho (~¥210, frequent till ~22:00) — or the 20-min flat walk up Hyakumangoku-odori, or a ¥900 taxi.

stops.title: Check-out — bags to bell desk
stops.notes: bags to the bell desk — collected after breakfast on the way to the station

stops.title: Omicho Market crab breakfast
stops.notes: many crab stalls open 08:00; kobako-gani runs ¥5,000–12,000 for two
stops.blurb: Kanazawa’s 300-year-old covered market — winter snow-crab season at its peak in late December.
stops.transit: 3-min walk — Omicho Market is literally beside the hotel; crab counters open ~07:30.

stops.title: Kanazawa Station
stops.transit: 12-min walk from Omicho down Hyakumangoku-odori to Kanazawa Stn.

stops.title: Kyoto Station — Hachijo (south) side
stops.notes: alight here off the Thunderbird; Tsurugi + Thunderbird is one through-ticket, ~¥7,800 pp
stops.blurb: The Hokuriku extension plus the Thunderbird limited express — Kanazawa to Kyoto in under two hours.
stops.transit: Hokuriku Shinkansen (Tsurugi) → Tsuruga, ~45 min; cross the platform to the Thunderbird → terminates at Kyoto Stn, ~55 min (through-fare ~¥7,800 pp, one booking); off the train, follow the 八条口 Hachijo (south) exit signs, ~6 min through the station.

stops.title: Hotel luggage drop
stops.notes: Comfort ERA Kyoto Toji — 13-min flat walk to Kyoto Stn, 1 min to Kintetsu Toji
stops.transit: Out of the Hachijo (south) exit, head WEST along Hachijo-dori with the Shinkansen tracks on your right, then left down toward Toji — 13-min flat walk to the hotel door; lazier option: Kintetsu line from inside Kyoto Stn, 1 stop to Toji (~2 min, ¥160), hotel 1-min from the exit; bags to the 24h desk — the takkyubin suitcases from Tokyo should already be waiting (email ahead to confirm).

stops.title: Kyoto Station bus terminal, stand D2
stops.place: Kyoto Station bus terminal, stand D2
stops.transit: Walk back to Kyoto Stn (13 min — or Kintetsu Toji → Kyoto, 1 stop); stand D2 is outside the north (Karasuma/Tower) side.

stops.title: Kimono rental & fitting
stops.notes: WEAR YOUR DINNER OUTFIT HERE — shops locker your clothes while you’re in kimono; no hotel detour needed later
stops.blurb: Dressing in a rental kimono for an afternoon in the old lanes is one of Kyoto’s signature experiences.
stops.transit: City Bus 206 → Gojozaka, ~15 min, ¥230 pp, Suica OK — rental shops cluster up the Gojozaka slope. (Christmas-Eve queues at D2 are real; a ~¥1,500 taxi saves 20 min.)

stops.title: Kiyomizu-dera + Sanneizaka — in kimono, in daylight
stops.notes: moved BEFORE tea (Dec sunset 16:48) — golden-hour photos and the Sanneizaka shops still open
stops.blurb: Kyoto’s great wooden-stage temple above the city, reached through the preserved slope lanes of Sanneizaka.
stops.transit: 10-min uphill walk from the kimono shop — straight up Gojozaka/Chawanzaka to the gate; shoot Sanneizaka on the way down instead.

stops.title: Tea ceremony — warm, indoors at dusk
stops.notes: ASK JAY to rebook the tea slot from 14:50 to ~16:15 — indoors right as the light goes
stops.blurb: A traditional tea ceremony: whisked matcha, seasonal sweets, and the quiet choreography of the tea room.
stops.transit: 5-min walk down Sanneizaka to the tea house — dusk light on the lanterns en route.

stops.title: Return kimono — back in dinner clothes
stops.notes: undressing takes 15–20 min; you leave already dressed for dinner
stops.transit: 5-min walk back up to the shop; they locker your day clothes, so you change and go.

stops.title: Hotel Okura Kyoto — lobby breather
stops.notes: breathe in the lobby before dinner
stops.transit: Hail a taxi on the GO app (or Uber) from Higashioji-dori — ~10 min, ¥1,100–1,400 total to Kawaramachi-Oike.

stops.title: Christmas-Eve dinner — Tokiwa teppanyaki
stops.place: Hotel Okura Kyoto — Sky Restaurant Pittoresque
stops.notes: 17F skyline · Xmas course ¥25–45k pp (Hijiri ¥35k: lobster + wagyu + Noël dessert) · Pittoresque Eve = SOLD OUT, lunch only · book Tokiwa on TableCheck NOW, slots thinning
stops.blurb: Japan’s Christmas Eve ritual at its best: a French course dinner above the lights of Kyoto.
stops.transit: No transit — dinner is upstairs in the same building: elevator to the 17th floor, seated by 18:30; LO 20:00–20:30 leaves a 10-min walk to the 21:00 mass.

stops.title: Midnight Mass — Kawaramachi Cathedral
stops.notes: Japan's 'midnight' mass runs ~21:00–22:15 — arrive ~20:40 for seats; carols usually precede the service, so you miss nothing by skipping the earlier gathering. Non-Christians welcome; confirm +81 75-231-4785. (Station lights tonight impossible — they're slotted tomorrow 17:15.)
stops.blurb: Kyoto’s main Catholic cathedral, whose candlelit Christmas Eve services draw a full house each 24 December.
stops.transit: 4-min walk from the Okura — one block up Kawaramachi, cathedral on the same block. After it ends ~22:15, taxi home ~¥1,300.

stops.title: Back at the hotel
stops.notes: Hot bath — big sunrise start tomorrow (07:30).
stops.transit: Taxi from the cathedral on the GO app — ~12 min, ~¥1,300 total; buses have thinned by 22:00.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.notes: Comfort ERA Kyoto Toji — 13-min flat walk to Kyoto Stn, 1 min to Kintetsu Toji

stops.title: Kyoto Station, JR Nara line (platforms 8–10)
stops.transit: 13-min walk to Kyoto Stn (or Kintetsu Toji → Kyoto, 1 stop); the Nara-line platforms 8–10 are the south-east corner of the concourse.

stops.title: JR Inari Station — torii opposite the exit
stops.notes: the shrine's first torii is directly opposite this tiny station's exit
stops.blurb: Inari Station on the JR Nara Line sits directly opposite the first torii gate of Fushimi Inari Taisha, just two stops from Kyoto Station.
stops.transit: JR Nara Line local → Inari, 2 stops, 5 min, ¥150 pp — the shrine's first torii is directly opposite the tiny station exit.

stops.title: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine
stops.blurb: Fushimi Inari Taisha is the head shrine of the rice deity Inari, famed for nearly ten thousand vermilion torii gates tunnelling up its sacred mountain.

stops.title: JR Inari Station
stops.transit: Walk back down through the torii to JR Inari Stn, 3 min.

stops.title: Transit to Sanjusangendo / Higashiyama area
stops.transit: JR Nara Line 1 stop back to Tofukuji → Keihan Line (toward Demachiyanagi) 2 stops to Shichijo, then a 7-min walk east; ~20 min, ¥310 pp. (One taxi ~¥1,300 if legs object.)

stops.title: Sanjusangendo Temple & Kennin-ji Temple visit
stops.notes: Kennin-ji Temple is at 35.0004, 135.7735
stops.blurb: Sanjusangendo houses 1,001 gilded statues of Kannon in Japan's longest wooden hall, while nearby Kennin-ji, founded in 1202, is Kyoto's oldest Zen temple.

stops.title: Keihan Shichijo Station
stops.transit: 7-min walk back west to Keihan Shichijo Stn.

stops.title: Gion-Shijo Station (Keihan)
stops.notes: take exit 6 for Shijo-dori
stops.transit: Keihan Line (toward Demachiyanagi) → Gion-Shijo, 2 stops, 3 min, ¥170 pp.

stops.title: Gion Hanamikoji Street & Shirakawa Canal stroll
stops.notes: Shirakawa Canal (Gion Shirakawa) is at 35.0064, 135.7747
stops.blurb: Hanamikoji is the signature street of Gion, Kyoto's most famous geisha district, lined with centuries-old wooden ochaya teahouses where geiko and maiko still entertain.
stops.transit: 5-min walk from Gion-Shijo exit 6 along Shijo-dori — Hanamikoji opens on the right past the theatre.

stops.title: Gion bus stop (Higashioji-dori)
stops.transit: 4-min walk east to the Gion bus stop on Higashioji-dori.

stops.title: Kyoto Station — evening lights
stops.transit: City Bus 206 → Kyoto Stn, ~20 min, ¥230 pp — Christmas-night buses pack out; a ~¥1,500 taxi is the sane upgrade.

stops.title: Kyoto Station lights — staircase show + tree
stops.notes: final day of the display (runs to 22:00); watch one staircase LED cycle before the 18:00 train
stops.blurb: Kyoto Station’s 171-step grand staircase becomes a giant LED canvas each December, crowned by the station’s Christmas tree.
stops.transit: In-station: the grand staircase rises from the central concourse, west side — the light show runs on it.

stops.title: Dinner — Kyoto Ramen Koji (Station 10F)
stops.notes: You're already at the station for the lights — ten regional ramen shops one escalator up. Or swap for the 19:00 daiku concert (see day flag).
stops.transit: Elevator to 10F from the same concourse — Ramen Koji is the row of eight regional ramen shops.

stops.title: Hotel
stops.notes: Comfort ERA Kyoto Toji — 13-min flat walk to Kyoto Stn, 1 min to Kintetsu Toji
stops.transit: Out the Hachijo (south) side, down the Miyakomichi arcade and west along Hachijo-dori — 13-min flat walk home; early night on purpose: 07:30 start tomorrow.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.notes: Comfort ERA Kyoto Toji — 13-min flat walk to Kyoto Stn, 1 min to Kintetsu Toji

stops.title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) visit
stops.blurb: Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion, is a Zen temple whose top two floors are entirely covered in gold leaf, shimmering above its mirror pond since 1397.
stops.transit: Taxi from the hotel, ~20 min, ~¥2,600 total — on a Saturday morning it beats the packed 205 bus by half an hour of standing. GO app or the rank outside Kyoto Stn.

stops.title: Ryoan-ji Zen rock garden visit
stops.blurb: Ryoan-ji holds Japan's most famous Zen rock garden — fifteen stones in raked white gravel, arranged so no single viewpoint reveals all of them at once.
stops.transit: 1.6 km along Kinukake-no-michi: pleasant 20-min walk, 5-min taxi (~¥800), or bus 59 one stop.

stops.title: Randen Ryoanji Station
stops.transit: 10-min walk down from the rock garden to Randen Ryoanji Stn.

stops.title: Randen-Arashiyama terminus
stops.notes: the rattling little tram ride is part of the day
stops.transit: Randen tram: Kitano Line to Katabiranotsuji, cross-platform to the Arashiyama Line → the terminus. ~30 min, ¥250 pp flat — the rattling little tram is part of the day.

stops.title: Togetsukyo Bridge stroll
stops.blurb: Togetsukyo, the 'Moon Crossing Bridge', has spanned the Katsura River for some four centuries and is the defining landmark of Kyoto's Arashiyama district.
stops.transit: 5-min walk from the Randen terminus straight ahead to the river — the bridge is the view.

stops.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove walk
stops.blurb: The Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is Kyoto's famed walking path through soaring green bamboo, whose creaking stalks are officially listed among Japan's 100 soundscapes.
stops.transit: 8-min walk north past Tenryu-ji's gate — enter the grove from the temple's north-gate side.

stops.title: JR Saga-Arashiyama Station
stops.transit: 10-min walk from the grove to JR Saga-Arashiyama Stn.

stops.title: Kyoto Station — back from Arashiyama
stops.transit: JR Sagano/San'in Line → Kyoto Stn, 12 min, ¥240 pp.

stops.title: Hotel rest & free time
stops.notes: Comfort ERA Kyoto Toji — 13-min flat walk to Kyoto Stn, 1 min to Kintetsu Toji
stops.transit: Out the Hachijo (south) exit, west along Hachijo-dori — 13-min walk home; feet up, tomorrow is a city switch.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.notes: Comfort ERA Kyoto Toji — 13-min flat walk to Kyoto Stn, 1 min to Kintetsu Toji

stops.title: Hotel check-out
stops.notes: Comfort ERA Kyoto Toji — 13-min flat walk to Kyoto Stn, 1 min to Kintetsu Toji

stops.title: Kyoto Station, JR Kyoto line (platforms 4/5)
stops.transit: 13-min walk back to Kyoto Stn with all the bags (or Kintetsu Toji → Kyoto, 1 stop).

stops.title: Osaka Station
stops.notes: head for the north-west side — the hotel is a 7-min walk
stops.blurb: The JR Special Rapid Service is the fast conventional train of the Kyoto-Osaka corridor, covering the distance in about 29 minutes with no reservation needed.
stops.transit: JR Kyoto Line Special Rapid from platforms 4/5 (toward Himeji) → Osaka Stn, 29 min, ¥580 pp — unreserved, tap Suica, window right side for the Yodo river.

stops.title: DEL style Shin-Umeda — luggage drop
stops.place: DEL style Osaka Shin-Umeda by Daiwa Roynet
stops.notes: DEL style Shin-Umeda (Daiwa Roynet, 2019) — ~7-min walk north-west of Osaka Stn; 24h desk stores bags before check-in
stops.transit: Out of Osaka Stn on the north-west side — the hotel is a ~7-min walk (Shin-Umeda); bags to the 24h desk, back to the station.

stops.title: Osaka Station, Loop line (platform 1)
stops.transit: Walk the 7 min back to Osaka Stn, Loop Line platform 1.

stops.title: Osakajokoen Station
stops.transit: JR Osaka Loop Line inner → Osakajokoen, ~10 min, ¥170 pp.

stops.title: Osaka Castle main keep visit
stops.blurb: Osaka Castle was built by unifier Toyotomi Hideyoshi in the 1580s as Japan's mightiest fortress; its rebuilt keep now houses a museum of the samurai era.
stops.transit: 10-min walk from Osakajokoen Stn through the park to the keep — last open day before the NY closure.

stops.title: Osakajokoen Station (Loop line)
stops.transit: 10-min walk back down through the park to Osakajokoen Stn.

stops.title: Free time around Osaka Station / Grand Front Osaka
stops.blurb: Grand Front Osaka is the flagship shopping and dining complex of the redeveloped Umeda district, packed with showrooms, boutiques and restaurants beside Osaka Station.
stops.transit: Loop Line back to Osaka Stn, ~10 min, ¥170 — Grand Front is across the north plaza.

stops.title: Umeda Sky Building & Kuchu Teien Observatory
stops.blurb: The Umeda Sky Building is a twin-tower landmark joined at the top by the Kuchu Teien 'Floating Garden' observatory, an open-air rooftop ring 173 metres up.
stops.transit: 10-min walk west from Grand Front under the JR tracks — the twin towers stay visible the whole way.

stops.title: Osaka Station City stroll
stops.blurb: Osaka Station City is the vast station complex at Umeda, uniting department stores, cinemas and rooftop plazas beneath a dramatic 180-metre glass dome roof.
stops.transit: 10-min walk back east into Osaka Station City.

stops.title: Yodobashi Umeda — Seiko & Orient Star
stops.notes: watch buying stop; 09:30–22:00; 2nd pass possible 28 Dec 09:30
stops.blurb: Yodobashi Umeda is one of Japan's largest electronics megastores, its watch floor stocking the full Seiko and Orient Star ranges alongside eight storeys of gadgets.
stops.transit: 10–12-min walk through Osaka Station City to the north gate — Yodobashi’s block faces it. Walking home after with the watches: ~9 min — out the north-west side past Grand Front, no metro needed.

stops.title: Back at the hotel — watches stowed
stops.place: DEL style Osaka Shin-Umeda by Daiwa Roynet
stops.transit: 9-min walk — out of Yodobashi's north face, west past Grand Front, straight to the hotel. No metro needed.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.place: DEL style Osaka Shin-Umeda by Daiwa Roynet

stops.title: Osaka Station, Loop line (platform 1)
stops.transit: Walk ~7 min from the hotel to Osaka Stn, Loop Line platform 1.

stops.title: Universal City Station
stops.transit: JR Loop inner → Nishikujo (5 min), cross the platform to the JR Yumesaki Line → Universal City (5 min). ¥190 pp. The 07:15 start is the queue-beater.

stops.title: Universal Studios Japan full-day experience
stops.notes: Express 7 'Mine Cart & Selection' slots run the day; at open ride Hollywood Dream then Flying Dinosaur standby. Studio Pass + Express bought by ~3 Dec.
stops.blurb: Universal Studios Japan is Osaka's blockbuster theme park, home to Super Nintendo World and the Wizarding World of Harry Potter.
stops.transit: 5-min walk down Universal CityWalk from the station — be AT the gates by 07:00: USJ opens 15–45 min before the posted time on peak days.

stops.title: Universal City Station
stops.transit: 5-min walk back down Universal CityWalk to the station.

stops.title: Back at the hotel (Shin-Umeda)
stops.place: DEL style Osaka Shin-Umeda by Daiwa Roynet
stops.transit: Yumesaki Line → Nishikujo → Loop Line to Osaka Stn, ~20 min, ¥190 pp; then the ~7-min walk home out the north-west side.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.place: DEL style Osaka Shin-Umeda by Daiwa Roynet

stops.title: Nishi-Umeda Station (Yotsubashi line)
stops.transit: Walk ~5 min from the hotel to Nishi-Umeda (Yotsubashi Line, blue Y — the closest subway).

stops.title: Kuromon Ichiba seafood market stroll
stops.blurb: Kuromon Ichiba, known as 'Osaka's kitchen', is a nearly 200-year-old covered market of some 150 stalls grilling scallops, crab and wagyu for strolling eaters.
stops.transit: Yotsubashi Line → Namba, direct 8 min, ¥240 pp; then a 10-min walk east along Sennichimae-dori to the market arcades.

stops.title: Dotonbori Canal & Shinsaibashi walk
stops.notes: Shinsaibashi shopping street is at 34.6739, 135.5012
stops.blurb: Dotonbori is Osaka's neon-lit canalside entertainment district, famed for the Glico running-man sign and giant mechanical crab, with the Shinsaibashi shopping arcade running north.
stops.transit: 10-min walk north through Nipponbashi — Dotonbori's neon canyon starts at the canal; Glico sign from Ebisubashi bridge.

stops.title: Namba Station (Midosuji line)
stops.transit: 5-min walk back over Ebisubashi to Namba Stn, Midosuji platforms.

stops.title: Dobutsuen-mae Station — Shinsekai side
stops.notes: exit 1 for the Jan-Jan Yokocho arcade
stops.transit: Midosuji Line → Dobutsuen-mae, 2 stops, 5 min, ¥190 pp — exit 1 for the Jan-Jan Yokocho arcade.

stops.title: Shinsekai Hondori Shopping Street stroll
stops.blurb: Shinsekai is Osaka's nostalgic early-1900s entertainment district, a retro warren of kushikatsu skewer joints and glowing signage beneath Tsutenkaku Tower.

stops.title: Tsutenkaku Tower visit
stops.blurb: Tsutenkaku is Shinsekai's beloved retro tower, a 1956 rebuild of a Paris-inspired 1912 original, with the lucky Billiken statue on its observation deck.
stops.transit: 2-min walk — the tower is the centre of the district.

stops.title: Dobutsuen-mae Station
stops.transit: 5-min walk back down Jan-Jan Yokocho to Dobutsuen-mae Stn.

stops.title: Back at the hotel
stops.place: DEL style Osaka Shin-Umeda by Daiwa Roynet
stops.transit: Midosuji 1 stop to Daikokucho, cross to the Yotsubashi Line → Nishi-Umeda, ~13 min, ¥240 pp; 5-min walk home.

stops.title: Breakfast
stops.place: DEL style Osaka Shin-Umeda by Daiwa Roynet

stops.title: Osaka Station
stops.transit: Walk ~7 min from the hotel to Osaka Stn.

stops.title: Shin-Osaka Station — Shinkansen gates
stops.notes: allow 20 min for the gate + ekiben run
stops.transit: JR Kyoto Line local, 1 stop, 4 min, ¥170.

stops.title: Tokyo Station — off the Nozomi
stops.notes: follow the Sobu Rapid (Yokosuka/Sobu) signs DOWN — deep platforms, ~10 min inside the station
stops.blurb: The Tokaido Shinkansen, opened in 1964, is the world's first high-speed railway, whisking passengers between Osaka and Tokyo in about two and a half hours.
stops.transit: Nozomi Shinkansen (reserved + the free oversized-luggage seats) → Tokyo, 2h27m · ¥14,720 pp (≈ ₹8,700); SmartEX early-bird saves ~¥2,500 pp — books 30 Nov.

stops.title: Tokyo hotel luggage drop
stops.notes: extension night — Jay to quote; placeholder near Tokyo Station
stops.transit: Off the Nozomi at Tokyo Stn, JR Yamanote/Keihin-Tohoku 1 stop to Kanda (2 min, ¥150 pp); APA Kanda Ekimae is a 3-min walk from the station; bags to the desk.

stops.title: JR Kanda Station
stops.transit: 3-min walk back to JR Kanda.

stops.title: Marunouchi + Hibiya illuminations walk
stops.blurb: Marunouchi Naka-dori is Tokyo's elegant tree-lined boulevard beside the station, whose champagne-gold winter illumination of over a million LEDs adjoins the Hibiya district's displays.
stops.transit: JR 1 stop to Tokyo Stn, Marunouchi side — Naka-dori's champagne-gold lights run 1.2 km to Hibiya; walk it as the light fades.

stops.title: Tokyo Station, JR Chuo line
stops.transit: Back into Tokyo Stn — the Chuo Line platforms are the high ones (1/2).

stops.title: Nakano Broadway — optional vintage safari
stops.notes: optional; call Jack Road 03-3386-9399; building closes Jan 1
stops.blurb: Nakano Broadway is Tokyo's legendary subculture mall, a 1966 arcade crammed with anime collectibles, manga and some of the city's best vintage-watch dealers.
stops.transit: JR Chuo Rapid → Nakano, direct 18 min, ¥230 pp — Broadway is 5 min up the Sun Mall arcade from the North exit.

stops.title: JR Nakano Station
stops.transit: 5-min walk back down the Sun Mall arcade to JR Nakano Stn.

stops.title: Dinner
stops.transit: Chuo Rapid direct back to Kanda, ~18 min, ¥230 — dinner in the izakaya alleys under the Kanda tracks.

stops.title: Lie-in + brunch
stops.notes: booked base — Kanda, 1 JR stop from Tokyo Stn

stops.title: JR Kanda Station
stops.transit: 3-min walk from the hotel to JR Kanda.

stops.title: Meiji Jingu — hatsumode via forest approach
stops.notes: 1.5–2 h queue expected
stops.blurb: Meiji Jingu is Tokyo's grandest Shinto shrine, enshrining Emperor Meiji within a 100,000-tree planted forest and drawing Japan's largest hatsumode crowds each New Year.
stops.transit: JR Chuo Rapid → Shinjuku (~13 min), cross to the Yamanote, 2 stops → Harajuku (~¥230); the quiet north forest approach starts 8 min from the West exit.

stops.title: Meiji-jingumae Station (Chiyoda line)
stops.transit: 8-min walk back out of the shrine forest to Meiji-jingumae Stn (Chiyoda Line).

stops.title: Tokyo Skytree — first night view
stops.notes: ¥3,100 advance; open to 22:00. The ascent we saved — Day 2 was base-only, tonight is the first view from the deck.
stops.blurb: Tokyo Skytree is Japan's tallest structure at 634 metres, a broadcasting tower with twin observation decks offering panoramic views across the Kanto plain to Mt. Fuji.
stops.transit: Chiyoda Line 1 stop to Omotesando, cross-platform to the Hanzomon Line — it through-runs all the way to Oshiage, Skytree's basement. ~35 min, ¥260 pp.

stops.title: Dinner
stops.transit: Zero transit — dinner is inside Solamachi, the mall under the tower.

stops.title: Oshiage Station (Asakusa line)
stops.transit: Escalators down — Skytree's basement is Oshiage station.

stops.title: Back at the hotel — night in
stops.transit: Toei Asakusa Line 2 stops to Asakusa, cross to the Ginza Line → Kanda direct; ~25 min, ~¥400 pp; 3-min walk home.

stops.title: Breakfast & out the door
stops.notes: konbini breakfast — be in the Palace security line by 08:15

stops.title: JR Kanda Station
stops.transit: 3-min walk from the hotel to JR Kanda.

stops.title: Imperial Palace Ippan Sanga — Nijubashi Main Gate
stops.notes: 2027 notice due late Dec
stops.blurb: Ippan Sanga is one of only two days a year the Imperial Palace's inner grounds open, as the Emperor and family greet the public from the Chowa-den balcony.
stops.transit: JR 1 stop to Tokyo Stn (2 min, ¥150), then a 10-min walk across Marunouchi to the Nijubashi plaza — in the security line by 08:15 with IDs; no big bags.

stops.title: Lunch
stops.transit: 10-min walk back into Marunouchi — Naka-dori or the KITTE building for lunch.

stops.title: Farewell dinner
stops.transit: 15-min walk down Harumi-dori into Ginza — or Marunouchi Line Tokyo → Ginza, 1 stop, ¥180.

stops.title: Ginza Station (Ginza line)
stops.transit: 3-min walk from Kabukiza to Ginza Stn.

stops.title: Back at the hotel — night in
stops.transit: Ginza Line (toward Asakusa) → Kanda, direct ~8 min, ¥180 pp; 3-min walk home.

stops.title: Slow breakfast — no alarm
stops.notes: booked base — Kanda, 1 JR stop from Tokyo Stn
stops.blurb: The one unhurried morning of the trip — the 10:10 flight moved to tomorrow and bought this whole day back.

stops.title: JR Kanda Station
stops.transit: 3-min walk from the hotel to JR Kanda.

stops.title: Converse Store Harajuku — Cat Street
stops.notes: Japan-licensee flagship — Made-in-Japan + Addict lines not sold outside Japan; NY sales still on; confirm 3 Jan hours (~11:00–20:00)
stops.blurb: Converse Japan is a separate licensee from Nike's Converse, and this Cat Street flagship (opened 2024) carries the Made-in-Japan and Addict lines you cannot buy outside the country.
stops.transit: JR Chuo Rapid → Shinjuku (~13 min), Yamanote 2 stops → Harajuku (¥230); exit toward Omotesando, Cat Street is 6 min down.

stops.title: Cat Street & Omotesando stroll — lunch
stops.notes: White Atelier BY CONVERSE (custom prints) is 5 min away if the flagship lights a fire; afternoon stays open
stops.transit: You're on it — Cat Street runs from Harajuku toward Shibuya; lunch anywhere along it, then loop back up to Omotesando.

stops.title: Omotesando Station (Ginza line)
stops.transit: Loop back up Cat Street to Omotesando Stn (orange G).

stops.title: Ginza NY-sale stroll — direct from Omotesando
stops.notes: Ginza Line, Omotesando → Ginza direct ~15 min. Hatsu-uri sales still on 3 Jan: Uniqlo NY sale, Ginza Six rooftop, Muji flagship, deep Itoya, fukubukuro if any left.
stops.blurb: Ginza is Tokyo's polished luxury quarter; in the first days of January its department stores run hatsu-uri new-year sales and sell fukubukuro lucky bags.
stops.transit: Ginza Line (toward Asakusa) → Ginza, direct 15 min, ¥210 pp — surfacing right at the 4-chome crossing for the hatsu-uri sales.

stops.title: Ginza Station (Ginza line)
stops.transit: Back under the 4-chome crossing to Ginza Stn.

stops.title: Last-night dinner — open
stops.notes: pick the farewell meal in December; pack tonight — 06:15 start tomorrow
stops.transit: Ginza Line (toward Asakusa) → Kanda, ~8 min, ¥180 pp; 3-min walk home — pack tonight, bags close at 23:00.

stops.title: Breakfast, check-out & luggage
stops.notes: booked base — Kanda, 1 JR stop from Tokyo Stn

stops.title: Private transfer to Narita
stops.notes: Tax-free customs confirmation BEFORE security: iPhone + receipts in hand luggage, refund (~¥23,200) releases after the check — budget 20–30 min. Also the watches' tax refunds.
stops.transit: Pre-booked private car, 10:15 pickup at the hotel entrance — ~75 min to Narita T2 departures. Fallback: JR 1 stop to Tokyo Stn + Narita Express (~55 min), clumsier with all the bags.

stops.title: Narita T2 — check-in + tax-free customs
stops.notes: check-in closes ~13:25; watches, boxes and receipts in hand at customs before bag drop
stops.blurb: Japan's tax-free refund is validated at customs with the goods physically present — the watch boxes ride in the cabin bag.

stops.title: CX527 departure — HYD via HKG, home 00:50
stops.notes: TICKETED: CX527 NRT 14:25 → HKG 18:55, CX601 HKG 21:05 → HYD 00:50 (Tue 5 Jan)

stops.title: Konbini breakfast — pace yourself, big day
stops.notes: NYE runs till 01:00 — eat, hydrate, layers ready

stops.title: JR Kanda Station
stops.transit: 3-min walk from the hotel to JR Kanda.

stops.title: Yurakucho Station
stops.transit: JR Yamanote (toward Tokyo/Shinagawa) 4 stops → Yurakucho, ~8 min, ¥170 pp.

stops.title: teamLab Planets TOYOSU — barefoot digital art
stops.notes: BOOK NOW at teamlabplanets.dmm.com — 09:00 slot, ~¥3,800–4,900 pp (dynamic); 31 Dec hours 08:00–20:00; barefoot + knee-deep warm water (shorts/lockers provided). Closes end-2027 — this trip is the window.
stops.blurb: A body-immersive digital-art museum you walk through barefoot — wading knee-deep through koi-lit water, drifting orchid gardens and mirror-infinity light rooms. Tokyo’s best date museum.
stops.transit: Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line (toward Shin-Kiba) → Toyosu, ~9 min, ¥180 pp; exit 7, then a 10-min waterfront walk (or Yurikamome 1 stop to Shin-Toyosu, 3-min walk).

stops.title: Ikebukuro Station
stops.transit: Yurakucho Line DIRECT Toyosu → Ikebukuro, ~37 min, ¥280 pp — one seat, no transfer; grab onigiri at Toyosu before boarding.

stops.title: Avengers: Doomsday — IMAX GT Laser
stops.notes: Tickets drop ~28–29 Dec 00:00 JST on cinemasunshine.co.jp — pick the 字幕 (subtitled) ~14:00 show, IMAX GT Laser (Japan’s biggest screen), ~¥2,900–3,600 pp.
stops.blurb: Japan’s largest IMAX GT Laser screen, four blocks from Ikebukuro — Doomsday on the format it was shot for, on New Year’s Eve.
stops.transit: 8-min walk from Ikebukuro East exit up Sunshine 60 street.

stops.title: Back at the hotel — rest before midnight
stops.notes: nap + warm layers; konbini dinner — Zojoji is a cold 3 hours
stops.transit: JR Yamanote from Ikebukuro (toward Tokyo) → Kanda, ~16 min, ¥210 pp; 3-min walk.

stops.title: JR Kanda Station
stops.transit: 3-min walk from the hotel to JR Kanda.

stops.title: Zojoji Temple — joya-no-kane + midnight, Tokyo Tower backdrop
stops.blurb: Zojoji is the Tokugawa shoguns' family temple, founded in 1393, whose forecourt beneath the lit Tokyo Tower is the classic stage for New Year's Eve bell-ringing.
stops.transit: JR Yamanote (toward Tokyo/Shinagawa) → Hamamatsucho, ~12 min, ¥170 pp; exit toward Tokyo Tower, 10-min walk up to Zojoji. Arrive 22:00–22:30 for a bell-queue spot.

stops.title: JR Hamamatsucho Station
stops.transit: 10-min walk back down from Zojoji (Tokyo Tower behind you) to JR Hamamatsucho.

stops.title: Kanda Station — off the all-night Yamanote
stops.transit: The ALL-NIGHT Yamanote straight back to Kanda — direct, no transfer, ~12 min, ¥170 pp. (The Toei subway does NOT run overnight.)

stops.title: Back at the hotel — Happy New Year 🎍
stops.transit: 3-min walk from Kanda station — door at ~00:50. Happy New Year. 🎍
